top5.title: AI Stocks Fall After the U.S. Elections
top5.description: The Nasdaq fell 5.5%, while several chipmakers dropped more than 9% or by double digits. Wall Street fears a slowdown in data centers after the adoption of numerous local measures aimed at restricting them.
top5.why: The 5.5% Nasdaq drop and sharp declines in AI-related stocks signal that election-driven resistance to data-center expansion could materially raise infrastructure costs and slow the AI buildout.

top5.title: Apple beats forecasts with record quarterly results
top5.description: Apple generated 114.5 billion dollars in revenue in the fourth quarter of 2026, beating Wall Street forecasts and its previous quarterly record from the 2020 holiday season.
top5.why: Apple’s record $114.5 billion quarter, above expectations, demonstrates continued strength in its core business and provides a major market benchmark for consumer technology demand.

top5.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber, specialized in exploit research
top5.description: OpenAI is launching GPT-6 Cyber, with improved exploit research capabilities and a higher API price than Anthropic and Google.
top5.why: OpenAI’s launch of GPT-6 Cyber highlights the accelerating commercialization of AI for exploit research, raising both cybersecurity risks and competitive pressure on model providers.

top5.title: Beijing Blocks SoftBank’s Acquisition of ABB’s Robotics Division
top5.description: China vetoed SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division through its foreign investment oversight body. The decision highlights the growing strategic importance of industrial robots.
top5.why: China’s veto of SoftBank’s acquisition of ABB’s robotics division shows that industrial robotics is becoming a strategic asset subject to increasingly aggressive geopolitical controls.

top5.title: Google will disable its AI services for students by default
top5.description: Google plans to disable its AI services for students by default next year, at schools’ request. The measure will include Google Search, which is considered an AI product.
top5.why: Google’s decision to disable AI services for students by default at schools’ request shows how education customers and regulators are pushing vendors toward stricter controls on generative AI.
